header: THE "UTILITY SERVICES" TAB OF THE USER GUIDE (text and data; the screen is src/components/help/UtilityServicesTab.tsx). A Utility Service is one of the helpers the app offers beside its main search (circulars, EDS, employees, departments, holidays, hospital, PAX, announcements and sites): the day's news, a price, the weather, a train, a calculator, the meaning of a number plate. They are auxiliary: they give something useful at once and do not look into the intranet's own records. I asked (17 Nov 2026) for them to have a tab of their own, with the words that open each one shown up front. The prose of every service is the prose they had in the introduction of the Sample questions tab (moved here, not changed). `type` is the words to type for a service (a SHORT or LONG command of the "What to type" list, so each is already tested against the real detector; src/lib/help/utilityServices.selftest.ts checks that every one of them is on that list and that no utility of that list is left out of the services).

doc: What these services cannot do yet, said plainly.

behaviours: the tab is called Utility Services; the lead calls them a host of Utility Services given to help employees in many different ways, says they are auxiliary, and says each has a bold name and the words that open it
two steps say how to get a service: click or type the words, press Enter (a sum, a conversion, a PIN code or a ward show as you type)
every topic of the registry has a word in the table above (so a new tool cannot be forgotten)
every topic of the registry is named in the Utility Services
it says the one-year graphs exist (fuel, gold and silver, dollar-rupee)
every service has a bold name and a detail, and none is listed twice; none is a main feature of the first tab
every service, or every part of a service that has parts, shows the words that open it (a service with parts carries them on its parts, not on itself)
every word shown is on the 'What to type' list, which the quick-reference test runs through the real detector (so each really opens the service)
each service's words come from the group of the list that is about it (news, live, calculators, Durgapur, DSP story, steel, vehicles)
every utility group of the 'What to type' list (calculators, vehicles, live, Durgapur, steel, DSP story, news) is represented among the words of the services
each service shows the words as a short command or a value to type (no word has a slash, which is the separator on the 'What to type' list), and no word is shown twice
the Calculators line names the command and says Enter opens a menu
every tool of the calculators menu is named in that line (a new tool cannot be forgotten)

the railway entry names BOTH stations as two tabs, Durgapur (DGR) and Asansol Junction (ASN), and says in brief WHY Asansol is there: trains that pass Durgapur without stopping, and trains that stop at Asansol but do not come to Durgapur, which a person at Durgapur can only take from Asansol

the railway, steel and AICPI entries are short (each under 450, 300 and 350 characters) and keep their facts: the two stations and why Asansol; the Ministry's prices, DSP's capacity, the companies and the world's production; the DA, MoSPI's index and the Reserve Bank's limit

the Vehicles entry has five numbered sub-titles, in order: National number plate, Tyre and rim specifications, EV cars: battery and charger (AC and DC) specifications, Engine power: PS, bhp and kW, VIN (vehicle identification number), simplified

the engine-power part gives the three units (bhp, PS, kW), says an electric car is described by two numbers (the battery in kWh, the size of its tank and the range; the power in kW, the actual power of the motor or motors turning the wheels), and says makers print bhp or PS beside kW

the number-plate part says it is the all-India BH-series plate and no longer carries the VIN; the tyre part names a tyre and a wheel marking; the EV part names kWh, kW, Blade, AC and DC, CCS2 and C-rate and points to the guide tab

the VIN part says what a VIN is (17 characters, on the chassis and in the papers, never I, O or Q), the three blocks (3 for country and maker, 6 for the type in the maker's own code, 8 for year, plant and serial), the year character (10th: K is 2019), and what to type

the limits say train fares are approximate and saved (until 13 December 2026), that CPI and inflation are MoSPI's saved data, that nearby EV charging stations are not there yet, that the flights and trains are timetables, and that nothing typed in a calculator is saved
the limits call them Utility Services: any words can open one, and only the typed line goes to Gemini, never a figure entered in a service, an ID or a name
no 'Good to know' point is long: each is under 400 characters
the utility tab's sample questions block (calculators, converters and live cards) is the data file's TOOLS_SECTION and is not empty
